title: Pro-etale lisse monodromy on a connected normal scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected Noetherian separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Assume that every local ring of $X$ is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and let $\Pi=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar x)$ be the profinite etale fundamental group [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $X$, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$, the limit of the constant pro-etale sheaves of rings [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. A lisse module means a sheaf module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] pro-etale locally free of finite rank, allowing rank zero.

There is an $E$-linear equivalence $\Phi_X$ from lisse $E_X$-modules to finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces with jointly continuous $\Pi$-action and equivariant linear maps, where the vector spaces have the product $\ell$-adic topology in any basis. This equivalence is normalized on finite integral monodromy as follows. If $V$ is such a representation and $\Lambda\subset V$ is any $\Pi$-stable finite free $A$-submodule with $E\otimes_A\Lambda\cong V$ and continuous restricted action for its $\varpi$-adic topology, let $F_n$ be the finite locally constant etale sheaf corresponding to $\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda$ under [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1), with transitions corresponding to quotient maps. For the comparison inverse image $\nu_X^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], set $N_\Lambda=\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*F_n$, a lisse $B_X$-module by [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison]. Then $\Phi_X(N_\Lambda[1/\varpi])\cong V$ naturally in lattice-preserving equivariant maps. In particular, if $\Phi_X(L)\cong V$, full faithfulness gives $N_\Lambda[1/\varpi]\cong L$.

source.place: Section 7.4 standing hypotheses; Lemmas 7.4.7 and 7.4.10, pp. 70–71; integral normalization from Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), pp. 59–60 and the first sentence of the proof of Lemma 7.4.7. Normality supplies geometric unibranchness by Stacks properties.tex Tag 0BQ3, lemma-normal-geometrically-unibranch.

proof.text: First compare the coefficient conventions, rather than treating a discrete constant $A$-sheaf as completed coefficients. By [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-reduction-equivalence], the continuous-function coefficient sheaf $A_X$ is canonically $\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_X=B_X$, and $A_X[1/\ell]=E_X$ in the continuous-function convention. Since $\ell$ and $\varpi$ are nonzero elements of the maximal ideal of the discrete valuation ring $A$, [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr](5) writes $\ell=u\varpi^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e>0$. Thus localization at either element gives the same sheaf, and the present $B_X[1/\varpi]$ agrees with that $E_X$. All subsequent coefficient changes use these canonical isomorphisms.

The scheme is quasi-compact by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], its closed subsets satisfy the descending-chain condition. Consequently [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] makes every subset of $|X|$ quasi-compact; in particular intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact, which verifies quasi-separatedness. Apply the first assertion of [lem-sfb-etale-local-monodromy-realization] to this connected qcqs, topologically Noetherian $X$ and the specified geometric point. It gives an $E$-linear fully faithful functor $J_X$ from the required continuous representations into lisse $E_X$-modules. Its integral normalization uses precisely the finite-level equivalence in the question. It remains to prove essential surjectivity; the etale-local realization clause of that node alone would not suffice.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), and the integral case of Lemma 7.4.7

proof.text: Fix a lisse $E_X$-module $L$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant] using step 1's coefficient identifications. Its sheaf $\mathscr L_L$ parametrizes integral lisse lattices together with their specified rational identification with $L$. On a pro-etale trivialization $L=E^r$, this sheaf is the constant sheaf with set $\operatorname{GL}_r(E)/\operatorname{GL}_r(A)$. This set contains the identity coset, including for $r=0$. Thus $\mathscr L_L$ is locally constant and has sections on a pro-etale covering. No global basis of $L$ is chosen.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), lattice-class sheaf and its coset trivialization

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-normal-locally-constant-finite-section] to $F=\mathscr L_L$. Its normal-local-ring, connectedness, nonemptiness and Noetherian hypotheses are exactly assumptions on $X$; local constancy and local nonemptiness were proved in step 3. We obtain a finite etale surjection $p:Y\to X$ and a section of $\mathscr L_L(Y)$. By the definition of that sheaf's sections, this section is an isomorphism class with a representative $(M,\alpha)$, where $M$ is integral lisse on $Y$ and $\alpha:M[1/\varpi]\simeq p^{-1}L$.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.9 and proof of Lemma 7.4.10, applied to the lattice-class sheaf

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-finite-etale-descent] for this $p$ and $(M,\alpha)$. The space $|X|$ is Noetherian by step 2, $p$ is finite etale and surjective by step 4, and $L,M$ are locally finite free with the specified rational identification. That theorem supplies an integral lisse $B_X$-module $M_0$ and $M_0[1/\varpi]\simeq L$. It does not require the specified lattice $M$ to carry descent data, and we do not assert that $M_0$ pulls back to $M$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, first paragraph, finite-etale lattice descent

proof.text: By [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison], $M_0$ corresponds to a normalized tower $(F_n)$ of finite locally free $A/\varpi^n$-module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, with $M_0\simeq\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*F_n$. Apply [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1) to each finite ring $A/\varpi^n$ (finiteness is part of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]). Let $\Lambda_n=(F_n)_{\bar x}$ with its finite discrete continuous $\Pi$-action. The finite-level equivalence is compatible with coefficient extension, so normalization gives $\Lambda_{n+1}/\varpi^n\Lambda_{n+1}\simeq\Lambda_n$, equivariantly. Each $\Lambda_n$ is finite free, since $F_n$ is finite locally free. By [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules](1), $\Lambda=\varprojlim_n\Lambda_n$ is finitely generated, $\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda\simeq\Lambda_n$, and its inverse-limit topology is its adic topology. The coordinatewise $\Pi$-action is jointly continuous: each coordinate of $\Pi\times\Lambda\to\Lambda$ factors through the continuous action on the finite discrete $\Lambda_n$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1) and the integral case at the start of the proof of Lemma 7.4.7

proof.text: The module $\Lambda$ is torsion-free. Indeed, if $\varpi\lambda=0$, its image in the free $A/\varpi^n$-module $\Lambda_n$ lies in $\varpi^{n-1}\Lambda_n$. For every fixed $k$, reducing from any $n>k$ makes that image zero in $\Lambda_k$; hence all coordinates of $\lambda$ vanish. Repeating this rules out $\varpi$-power torsion, and every nonzero element of $A$ is a unit times a power of $\varpi$ by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. This node also says $A$ is a DVR. Apply [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] to conclude that $\Lambda$ is finite free. Put $V=E\otimes_A\Lambda$. A basis of $\Lambda$ identifies $V$ with $E^r$ and $\Lambda$ with $A^r$; the sets $\varpi^{-k}\Lambda$ are open and exhaust $V$. On each such set the action is the rescaled continuous action on $\Lambda$, so the action $\Pi\times V\to V$ is jointly continuous. The submodule $\Lambda\subset V$ is therefore an invariant finite free lattice of the kind in the question.

source.place: Integral representation in the proof of Lemma 7.4.7, with the torsion-free inverse-limit check written out

proof.text: The finite-level equivalences identify $F_n$ with the sheaf corresponding to $\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda$, with the quotient transition maps. Thus the normalization of [lem-sfb-etale-local-monodromy-realization] gives $J_X(V)\simeq (\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*F_n)[1/\ell]\simeq M_0[1/\varpi]\simeq L$. The middle isomorphism is the inverse of reduction in [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison], and step 1 identifies the two localizations. This proves essential surjectivity for the same fully faithful $J_X$, rather than constructing a separate functor for each lattice.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), integral case of Lemma 7.4.7 and normality input of Lemma 7.4.10

proof.text: Construct an inverse $\Phi_X$ explicitly: for each $L$ choose $V_L$ and $a_L:J_X(V_L)\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ as above, and define $\Phi_X(f)$ to be the unique map whose image under $J_X$ is $a_{L'}^{-1}fa_L$. Full faithfulness gives uniqueness, preserves identities and composition, and makes this functor $E$-linear. The $a_L$ give one natural inverse isomorphism; full faithfulness gives the other. Hence $\Phi_X$ is the required $E$-linear equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 7.4.7, assembling full faithfulness and essential surjectivity

proof.text: Finally let $(V,\Lambda)$ be any representation and stable lattice as in the question. The normalization of [lem-sfb-etale-local-monodromy-realization] is $J_X(V)\simeq N_\Lambda[1/\ell]$, naturally for lattice-preserving equivariant maps, and [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] ensures $N_\Lambda$ is integral lisse. Step 1 replaces $1/\ell$ by $1/\varpi$. Applying the inverse equivalence and its unit gives $\Phi_X(N_\Lambda[1/\varpi])\simeq V$ with exactly that naturality. If $\Phi_X(L)\simeq V$, full faithfulness lifts this isomorphism and its inverse to mutually inverse sheaf morphisms $N_\Lambda[1/\varpi]\simeq L$. All constructions include the zero module and the unique rank-zero lattice.

source.place: First sentence of proof of Lemma 7.4.7 and Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), integral normalization

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6), finite-cover descent in Lemma 6.8.13, integral case of Lemma 7.4.7, and geometric-cover argument in Lemma 7.4.10

Uses the existing normalized fully faithful representation functor, not its local conclusion, to isolate the genuinely new normal-base essential-surjectivity argument.
Uses the lattice-choice sheaf and its coset trivializations, valid over any scheme; the curve unit has no lattice-class theorem.
Descends existence of an integral lattice across the finite etale cover, without descent data on that lattice.
Uses the existing normalized integral reduction/inverse-limit equivalence and its rational realization.
Reconstructs the finite generated adic fibre from finite normalized reductions, with topology.
Converts the reconstructed finitely generated torsion-free integral fibre into a finite free lattice.
Supplies the DVR and unit-times-uniformizer factorization used for localization and torsion-freeness.
Checks topological Noetherianity from the precise ring-theoretic Noetherian hypothesis.
Checks quasi-separatedness via compactness of affine-open intersections.
